description: d3's `quantileSorted` ends `return value0 + (value1 - value0) * (i - i0)`, and it evaluates that product even when `i` lands exactly on a sample and the weight is zero. Returning `values[i0]` there is the obvious saving, exact for every finite column, and wrong for one holding an infinity: `(Infinity - 2) * 0` is **NaN**, not zero. Four samples and a three-colour range is the shape that reaches it — the cuts sit at `i = 1` and `i = 2` exactly — so the `wild` scale has thresholds `[1, NaN]` upstream and had `[1, 2]` here. A NaN cut point is not a missing one: it is a boundary every comparison fails, which sends a bisection left rather than right, and two of the four marks changed colour. The short circuit also hid a second slip, visible only in the same place: d3 reads `values[i0 + 1]` for the upper sample and this read `values[ceil(i)]`, which names the *same* sample again whenever the position is whole. `tame` is the identical shape with the infinity taken out, so the fixture says what the rule costs an ordinary chart, which is nothing; `between` has a four-colour range, where every cut falls between two samples and the interpolation itself is what is compared.

text.signal: datum.v + ' -> ' + scale('wild', datum.w) + '  ' + scale('tame', datum.w) + '  ' + scale('between', datum.w)
